problem:
Consider the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{3}(t)}$ of polynomials from $R[t],$ where

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=-1+t-2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=-2,\,{p}_{3}(t)=t-2{t}^{2}.
$$

If the set is linearly dependent, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}$ from a non-zero solution of ${x}_{1}\cdot {p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}\cdot {p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}\cdot {p}_{3}(t)=0.$

activity_context.topic_title: Linear Independence in Abstract Vector Spaces

feedback.problem:
Consider the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ of polynomials from $R[t],$ where

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t-4{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=3t-6{t}^{2}.
$$

If the set is linearly dependent, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{2}}{{x}_{1}}$ from a non-zero solution of ${x}_{1}\cdot {p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}\cdot {p}_{2}(t)=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If the set is linearly dependent, then there exist ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ not both zero such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=0.
$$

Otherwise, if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0,$ the set is linearly independent.

Substituting the given expressions for ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t)$ into the above equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2t-4{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(3t-6{t}^{2}) & =0 \\ (2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})t+(-4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The final equation is true for every $t$ if and only if 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding augmented matrix and reduce it to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ -4 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot column is the $1$st one. Hence, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the $1$st equation, we get

$$
2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Finally, for any ${x}_{2}\ne 0,$ we obtain 

$$
\frac{{x}_{2}}{{x}_{1}}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{(-\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2})}=-\frac{2}{3}.
$$
